topic: Scraped your rim on a curb? Here's how to tell cosmetic damage from a bent wheel.

beats.vo: Scraped your rim on a curb? Here's how to tell if it's just cosmetic — or something worse.
beats.visual: Macro shot of an alloy wheel rim outer edge with a shallow curb scuff, static camera, soft studio-style side light

beats.vo: A shallow scuff on the outer edge is usually cosmetic — it doesn't affect how the wheel holds air or spins true.
beats.visual: Two macro rim-edge compositions in sequence: shallow cosmetic scuff next to a deeper gouge, subtle crossfade, no on-screen text

beats.vo: The real warning signs are a wobble in the steering wheel, a rhythmic vibration at speed, or the tire slowly losing air near the rim edge.
beats.visual: Extreme macro, slow push-in on the tire-to-rim bead seal area, ambient shop lighting

beats.vo: A bent wheel can still hold air for weeks before it fails — don't wait for a blowout to find out.
beats.visual: Close-up of a tire pressure gauge read at a valve stem near the rim, static mounted camera, no hands in frame

beats.vo: Worth a quick look if you felt or heard anything. Stop by and we'll take a look.
